title: Sweep metal chips into a scrap trough with a bar, around a loose workpiece that must not move
instruction: Leave the loose blue workpiece exactly where it is, and keep every chip on the surface: using the yellow bar as a scraper, slide all eight metal chips across the plate and over its far edge into the scrap trough. Never lift a chip or pick one up.
context: Machinists clear chips off a fixture plate with a scraper, not by hand, while the part sits there unclamped; knocking it loses its setup. Sweeping tasks exist (Meta-World, RLBench); here chips sit beside, behind and in front of a loose part, so the tool must work around it.
setup: Station table. Coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and y = -0.305 (right); everything is in front of the left arm. Fixed: a dark grey steel plate 280 x 240 x 15 mm (x, y, z) spanning x 0.12 to 0.40 and y 0.10 to 0.34. Beyond its far edge is a scrap trough 40 mm wide (x 0.40 to 0.44) whose floor is the table top, 15 mm below the plate top; a red lip 10 mm thick and 30 mm tall (above the table) closes its far side (x 0.44 to 0.45, y 0.094 to 0.346), and two red end walls 6 mm thick and 30 mm tall close its ends (y 0.094 to 0.100 and 0.340 to 0.346). Loose, on the plate: a yellow aluminium bar 20 x 75 x 20 mm (81 g) lying with its length along y, centred at x 0.15, y 0.22; a blue acetal (POM) workpiece block 80 x 60 x 40 mm (270 g) standing upright, its 80 mm side along x, centred at x 0.30 and at y 0.15, 0.22 or 0.29; eight bare aluminium chips, 15 mm cubes (9 g each), lying square to the plate on a grid of cells at x 0.205 to 0.380 and y 0.125 to 0.325 in 25 mm steps, each at least 10 mm from the workpiece. A layout number picks the workpiece spot and the chip cells: the README lists layouts 0 to 9 and the rule for any number. The screenshot and the submitted runs use layout 2: workpiece at y 0.15; chips (x, y) at (0.380, 0.250), (0.205, 0.225), (0.380, 0.325), (0.380, 0.175), (0.280, 0.200), (0.205, 0.275), (0.305, 0.200), (0.305, 0.275). Real-world build: a steel plate or flat aluminium sheet on 15 mm spacers, a trough of folded sheet or printed PLA, a 25 mm cell grid and the workpiece's outline (plus a line 15 mm outside it) drawn on the plate. An overhead camera records the plate for the whole trial.
scoring: A chip is credited if it ends in the trough and was never lifted and never moved except by the bar. In the trough: its whole footprint inside the trough (between the plate edge, the lip and the end walls), still, and either its bottom at least 3 mm below the plate top (fallen in, even if propped or leaning) or resting on another chip that is itself in the trough. Lifted: at any moment its bottom more than 4 mm above the plate top, unless it rests on a chip that is itself on the plate (a chip riding on another while swept), or it is over the trough, lip or end walls. Moved without the bar: at any moment it slides or turns on the plate while more than 10 mm from the bar and not touching a moving chip that the bar is driving, directly or through other chips (this rules out pushing chips with the fingertips). Workpiece factor: 1.0 if at the end it is within 5 mm and 3 degrees of its start; 0.5 if within 15 mm; 0 if further, or if at any moment it moved more than 15 mm, was lifted more than 4 mm off the plate, tipped more than 5 degrees or left the plate. Score = credited chips / 8 x workpiece factor. Full score (1.0) is all eight chips credited and the workpiece within 5 mm and 3 degrees; the trial ends once that has held for 1 s. Real trial: the judge reviews the overhead video for each chip (never picked up, pinched or held off the plate; moving only while the bar, or a chip the bar is pushing, is against it) and for the workpiece (never lifted or tipped, never over the line drawn 15 mm outside its outline). After the arm stops, measure the workpiece's offset from its outline with a ruler or caliper: shift is the move of its centre; turn is the difference between the offsets at the two ends of an 80 mm side (3 degrees is 4.2 mm). Count the chips in the trough from a top photo. Picking chips up and dropping them in scores 0; so does pushing them with the fingers, and moving the workpiece aside and back.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Take the chips out of the trough, set the next trial's layout from the README's table (workpiece spot and eight chip cells, using the grid drawn on the plate), put the workpiece on its outline and the bar back at its start, and start a new overhead video.
fidelity: Approximate. Every object is a rigid box with one rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), so chips slide less freely than steel swarf; chips are 15 mm aluminium cubes, not curls. The trough floor is the table, 15 mm below the plate. The lift and bar-contact rules are read from object poses every step, where a real trial reads them from overhead video. The workpiece is a light acetal block, so a bump moves it more easily than a steel part.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (layout 2, all 3,000 steps); demo: 1.0 (layout 2, 829 steps)
